title: Controlled Components
description: Learn how to control form inputs with React state.

data.text: In React, form inputs can be **controlled** or **uncontrolled**. Controlled components have their value managed by React state, making them predictable, easy to validate, and simple to reset.
A controlled input's value is driven by React state. An uncontrolled input manages its own internal state like a standard DOM element.

cards.title: Controlled
cards.description: React state is the single source of truth for the input value.
pros: Easy to disable, reset, or conditionally enable
Predictable — React state and input are always in sync
cons: Requires an onChange handler for every input

cards.title: Uncontrolled
cards.description: The DOM manages the input value; React reads it via a ref.
cons: Harder to validate in real time
Harder to programmatically reset or modify

data.text: Bind the input's `value` to state and update that state on every `onChange`. The component becomes the single source of truth.

data.title: Controlled Text Input
Read-Only Trap
data.text: If you set `value` on an input without `onChange`, the field becomes read-only. Always pair a controlled input with a change handler.
Checkboxes use `checked` (a boolean) instead of `value`. Read the checked state from `e.target.checked`.

data.title: Controlled Checkbox
data.content: Binding a checkbox to boolean state

data.text: Select dropdowns also use `value` to control the selected option.

data.title: Controlled Select

data.text: Use the input's `name` attribute and computed property syntax to handle multiple fields with a single `onChange` function.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Profile Form
data.description: Create a controlled form with multiple inputs and live validation.
steps: Create a ProfileForm component with username, email, and bio fields.
Use a single state object and a single handleChange function.
Show an error message if the email is invalid as the user types.
Disable the submit button until all fields are valid.
data.expectedOutcome: A form with live validation that prevents submission of invalid data.

items.question: Are controlled components always better?
items.answer: For most forms, yes. They give you full control over validation, formatting, and submission. Use uncontrolled inputs for file inputs or when integrating with non-React libraries.

items.question: Why is my input not editable?
items.answer: You likely forgot to add onChange, or you set value to a state variable that never updates.

items.question: Can I mix controlled and uncontrolled inputs?
items.answer: Yes, but it is rare. A common exception is a file input, which must be uncontrolled.

items.question: Should I use a form library?
items.answer: For complex forms with many fields, consider React Hook Form or Formik. They reduce boilerplate while keeping inputs controlled.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Controlled inputs bind their value to React state via value and onChange.
Checkboxes use checked; selects use value.
A single handler can manage multiple inputs using the name attribute.
Always pair value with onChange to avoid read-only inputs.
data.takeaway: Controlled components put React in charge of form data. Next, you will explore advanced form handling patterns.
